insurer: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: As per Policy Schedule (Silver/Gold/Platinum; Individual/Family Floater/Family First variants)

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: “We will provide an additional re-fill amount of maximum up to 100% of the Base Sum Insured.”
great.explanation: An additional re-fill amount of up to 100% of the Base Sum Insured is provided. This effectively gives you extra Sum Insured in the same policy year after the base cover is used.

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: “Re-fill benefit Reinstate up to base Sum Insured. Applicable for same & different illness as well”
great.reference: Annexure II – Product Benefit Table (Silver/Gold/Platinum tables)
great.explanation: The Sum Insured can be reinstated up to the base amount and is applicable for the same as well as different illnesses. This is stronger than restores that work only for unrelated illnesses.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-existing Disease (PED) ... shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months (under gold & platinum Plans)/ 36 months (under Silver Plans) of continuous coverage”
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are not covered for 24 months (Gold/Platinum) or 36 months (Silver). This is within the common market range of 2–4 years.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of any Illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an Accident”
good.explanation: Illness claims are not covered in the first 30 days from the policy start, except for accidents. This is a standard waiting period in retail health insurance.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: “For all Insured Persons who are above 45 years of Age ... Expenses related to the treatment of the listed conditions ... shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage”
good.explanation: For insured persons above 45 years, listed conditions/procedures are not covered for the first 24 months. This is a typical specific-illness waiting period.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “We will pay ... Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses only for period up to 60 days immediately preceding the Insured Person’s admission”
good.explanation: Pre-hospitalization medical expenses are covered up to 60 days before admission. This helps pay for consultations and tests leading up to hospitalization.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “We will pay Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses only for up to 90 days immediately following the Insured Person’s discharge”
good.explanation: Post-hospitalization medical expenses are covered up to 90 days after discharge. This supports follow-up treatment and medicines during recovery.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: “Room rent Shared Room or 1% of the Base Sum Insured per day”
bad.reference: Annexure II – Product Benefit Table (Individual & Family Floater – Silver Plan)
bad.explanation: Room rent is limited to a Shared Room or 1% of the Base Sum Insured per day. Choosing a higher room category can significantly increase your out-of-pocket costs.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: “If the Insured Person is admitted in a Hospital room where the room category opted or Room Rent incurred is higher than the eligibility as specified in the Policy Schedule, then We shall be liable to pay only a pro-rated portion of the total Associated Medical Expenses ... (Eligible Room Rent limit / Room Rent actually incurred) * total Associated Medical Expenses”
bad.explanation: If you take a room above your eligible category, the insurer pays only a pro-rated portion of associated medical expenses using the stated formula. This can reduce payouts across the whole bill, not just the room rent.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: “The expenses that are not covered or subsumed into room charges/ procedure charges/ costs of treatment are mentioned in Annexure VI”
bad.explanation: Consumables that are not covered (or not subsumed into other charges) are listed as exclusions in Annexure VI. This can lead to extra out-of-pocket costs for common hospital items.

bad.name: Restore Limit
bad.quote: “We will provide a re-fill amount only once in a Policy Year.”
bad.explanation: The re-fill amount is available only once in a policy year. After one restore is used, further claims in the same year may not get any additional top-up from this benefit.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: “The Insured Person will bear a predetermined percentage of the admissible claim amounts subject to the Co-payment option chosen by You in the Proposal Form and / or Information Summary Sheet”
bad.explanation: A co-pay applies based on the co-payment option chosen in the Proposal Form and/or Information Summary Sheet. This means you may have to bear a percentage of every admissible claim, so the exact co-pay must be checked in your schedule.

unclear.name: No Claim Bonus
unclear.quote: “Cumulative Bonus means any increase or addition in the Sum Insured granted by the insurer without an associated increase in premium.”
unclear.reference: Section 2.5 (Definition only; no non-resetting protection stated)
unclear.explanation: Only a definition of Cumulative Bonus is provided here, without stating the accrual rate or what happens to it after a claim. You need the benefit table/policy schedule to know how much bonus you can earn and whether it reduces or resets on a claim.

unclear.name: Cashless Network
unclear.quote: “The complete list of Network Providers is available on Our website and at Our branches”
unclear.explanation: The policy directs you to the insurer’s website/branches for the network hospital list but does not state a count. Cashless availability should be verified for your city and preferred hospitals before buying.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
